es: Sintetizar la información de un audio y de un texto: comparar lo que coincide, señalar las discrepancias y cerrar con una conclusión.

teaching.en: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper says it closes in July.
teaching.es: Según el informe de la radio, la biblioteca cierra en junio, mientras que el periódico dice que cierra en julio.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas contrasta dos fuentes: cada una con su dato, en una sola frase.
segments: According to the radio report, the library closes in
June, whereas the newspaper says it closes in July.
teaching.audioText: According to the radio report, the library closes in June, whereas the newspaper says it closes in July.

teaching.en: Both sources agree that the library is too small.
teaching.es: Las dos fuentes coinciden en que la biblioteca es demasiado pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: Both + fuentes en plural + verbo sin -s: señala una coincidencia.
teaching.audioText: Both sources agree that the library is too small.

teaching.en: Likewise, the radio figure and the newspaper figure show that visits fell last year.
teaching.es: Del mismo modo, la cifra de la radio y la del periódico muestran que las visitas cayeron el año pasado.
teaching.explanationEs: Likewise añade otra coincidencia. Figure = cifra o dato numérico.
segments: Likewise, the radio figure and the newspaper
figure show that visits fell last year.
teaching.audioText: Likewise, the radio figure and the newspaper figure show that visits fell last year.

teaching.en: There is a discrepancy: the radio says 400 visitors, but the newspaper gives 300.
teaching.es: Hay una discrepancia: la radio dice 400 visitantes, pero el periódico da 300.
teaching.explanationEs: Discrepancy = diferencia entre datos. Se nombra y luego se explica (¿quién habla? ¿cuándo?).
segments: There is a discrepancy: the radio says
teaching.audioText: There is a discrepancy: the radio says 400 visitors, but the newspaper gives 300.

teaching.en: The radio source is the library manager, so her figure may be more exact.
teaching.es: La fuente de la radio es la directora de la biblioteca, así que su cifra puede ser más exacta.
teaching.explanationEs: Evaluar la fuente: quién habla y qué sabe. Es parte de una buena síntesis.
segments: The radio source is the library manager,
so her figure may be more exact.
teaching.audioText: The radio source is the library manager, so her figure may be more exact.

teaching.en: Overall, the two sources agree on the problem, but they differ on the date.
teaching.es: En conjunto, las dos fuentes coinciden en el problema, pero difieren en la fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall abre la conclusión: resume coincidencias y diferencias en una frase.
segments: Overall, the two sources agree on the
problem, but they differ on the date.
teaching.audioText: Overall, the two sources agree on the problem, but they differ on the date.

prompt.es: ¿Qué relación hay entre las dos fuentes sobre la apertura de la piscina?

choices.text: They agree on the date.
They do not mention the date.
They show a discrepancy about the date.

feedback.es: La radio dice el 1 de mayo y el artículo el 15 de mayo: los datos no coinciden, así que hay una discrepancia sobre la fecha.

origin.text: Radio: The pool opens on 1 May. Article: The pool opens on 15 May.

prompt.es: Completa: «La radio dice junio, mientras que el periódico dice julio.»

feedback.es: Whereas contrasta dos datos de dos fuentes distintas en una sola frase.

hint.es: Es el conector de contraste que equivale a «mientras que».

origin.text: The radio says June, ___ the newspaper says July.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase de síntesis compara correctamente las dos fuentes?

choices.text: According to the radio, 400 people visited, whereas the article gives 300.
The radio and the article say 400 people visited.
According to the article, 400 people visited, and the radio says 300.

feedback.es: Cada cifra va con su fuente y el conector whereas marca el contraste. Las otras dos mezclan o invierten los datos.

hint.es: Cada cifra debe ir con su fuente.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y elige cómo se relacionan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: They agree on the number.
They show a discrepancy in the number.
They give the same date.

feedback.es: El audio dice doscientos niños y el periódico doscientos cincuenta: los datos no coinciden, hay una discrepancia en la cifra.

origin.audio: The manager says two hundred children joined the club this year.
origin.text: Newspaper: Two hundred and fifty children joined the club this year.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector o término con su función en la síntesis.

pairs.es: Diferencia entre datos de dos fuentes

feedback.es: Cada término cumple una función: coincidencia, contraste, diferencia entre datos y conclusión.

pairs.es: Diferencia entre datos de dos fuentes

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las dos fuentes coinciden en la cifra, pero no en la fecha.»

answer.text: The two sources agree on the figure but not on the date

feedback.es: Agree on introduce el punto de coincidencia y but not on señala la diferencia: la coincidencia y la discrepancia caben en una sola frase.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y elige en qué discrepan las dos fuentes.

choices.text: In the number of daily passengers.
In who runs the bus company.
In the start date of the new bus line.

feedback.es: El portavoz dice que la línea empieza en septiembre y el periódico dice octubre: esa es la discrepancia. Las dos fuentes calculan unos tres mil pasajeros al día.

origin.audio: The council spokesperson says the new bus line will carry about three thousand passengers a day from September.
origin.text: Newspaper: The new bus line starts in October. The transport company expects about three thousand passengers a day.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y elige qué añade el audio que no dice el texto.

choices.text: That the paths stay open in winter.
That the lake is closed in winter.
That the lake opens in November.

feedback.es: El sitio web solo informa del cierre del lago de noviembre a marzo; el audio añade que los senderos siguen abiertos todo el año.

origin.audio: The park guide says the lake is closed in winter, but the paths stay open all year.
origin.text: Website: The lake is closed from November to March.

prompt.es: Completa la síntesis: contraste, coincidencia y conclusión.

feedback.es: However abre el contraste entre las dos cifras, agree marca la coincidencia y Overall abre la conclusión.

sentences: According to the radio, 60 people came. ___, the newspaper says 80.
The two sources ___ that attendance fell.
___, the main problem is the same.

prompt.es: Escucha la radio, lee el artículo y escribe una síntesis comparando las dos fuentes.

answer.text: According to the radio, the playground will open in May, whereas the article says June. Both sources agree that it will cost about two hundred thousand pounds. However, only the article mentions that some neighbours worry about the noise. Overall, the sources agree on the cost but differ on the opening date.
accepted: According to the radio, the playground will open in May, whereas the article says June. Both sources agree that it will cost about two hundred thousand pounds. However, only the article mentions that some neighbours worry about the noise. Overall, the sources agree on the cost but differ on the opening date.

The radio and the article agree that the playground will cost about two hundred thousand pounds. There is a discrepancy about the date: the radio gives May, while the article gives June. In addition, only the article reports that some neighbours are worried about the noise. Overall, the main difference is the opening date.

feedback.es: Una buena síntesis compara en un párrafo: cada fuente con su dato, lo que coincide, lo que solo dice una fuente y una conclusión.

origin.text: Article: The council confirms that the playground will open in June. It will cost about two hundred thousand pounds. Some neighbours worry about the noise.
origin.audio: The mayor says the new playground will open in May, and it will cost two hundred thousand pounds. Local families welcome the idea.

prompt.es: Escucha, lee y elige qué datos coinciden.

choices.text: The length of the exam.
The day of the exam.
The room of the exam.

feedback.es: Ambas fuentes dicen que el examen es el martes; la duración no coincide (dos horas frente a noventa minutos).

origin.audio: The teacher says the exam is on Tuesday and lasts two hours.
origin.text: School website: The exam is on Tuesday and lasts ninety minutes.

choices.text: Both sources say profits fell.
Source A says sales fell, but Source B says they rose.
Both sources say sales rose ten per cent, and only Source B adds that profits fell.

feedback.es: La primera recoge lo que coincide (las ventas subieron un diez por ciento) y lo que solo dice la fuente B (los beneficios bajaron). Las otras inventan datos.

origin.text: Source A: Sales rose by ten per cent. Source B: Sales rose by ten per cent, but profits fell.

prompt.es: Completa: «Del mismo modo, las dos cifras muestran una caída.»

feedback.es: Likewise (o similarly) añade una coincidencia más entre las dos fuentes.
